ramp._note: Procedural waves past the authored ones (20) are templated from the last authored waves. Counts grow a little a wave and stop at count_cap (times the template's count); past that the rest goes into health so the field stays readable and the frame rate holds. Deep waves gain traits and commanders: commander_chance_per_wave x waves past start_wave (at most commander_chance_max) times the surge count, rounded, every wave (a roll per surge gave one wave none and the next four). Each template is scaled to the pool's mean health budget (count x health), so the wave after a gentle one isn't four times as hard. Health itself follows the climb below, the same curve for every wave.

climb._note: Every wave is harder than the last, from wave 1 (2026-10 balance pass). hp is (wave, health multiplier) points joined log-linearly, compounding at hp_growth_after past the last point; it applies to every enemy of every wave, authored or procedural, commanders included. Before this the authored waves stayed gentle to W20 and then compounded 18% a wave, a wall a full build hit around W30. Enemy damage grows damage_per_wave a wave. A leak costs leak_base + leak_per_wave x wave (commanders and bosses times their mult), capped at leak_cap_share of the Spire's full health (leak_cap_share_big for commanders and bosses), so one leak never ends a run. Ascendants keep their own share (ascendants.json). The Spire mends spire_mend_share of its full health when a wave clears. Leaks were 8 + 0.6 a wave with the Bruteforge Spire regenerating 4 a second: it was full at the start of every wave and one bad wave took all of it, so a run looked fine until it ended. Now a leak is 4 + 0.05 a wave (about 40 to empty a fresh Spire at W30) and the regeneration is slow: a defence that starts to fail drains the Spire over waves you can see.
climb._threat_note: AXIS answers a stronger BIT: every enemy's health is times 1 + (points / threat_scale) ^ threat_power for the perk-tree points owned, at most threat_cap (Climb.Threat, shown on the wave card): x1.2 at 36 points, x1.8 at 60, x3 at 80, x5 at 102. A tree's strength sits in its deep ranks and keystones; linear (1.75% a point) left a 36-point tree four waves behind a new account and a 102-point tree 14 to 20 waves ahead. A 100-point tree made the first 30 waves 3 to 20 times easier than the defence needed, so nothing ever threatened it.

economy._note: Money keeps pace with the climb. Kill bounties grow bounty_per_wave a wave. Past the authored waves the wave-clear bonus is bonus_after_authored x bonus_growth^(waves past). Resource nodes pay node_per_wave more a wave. Every wave clear pays interest_pct of banked Resources, capped at interest_cap_base + interest_cap_per_wave x wave (the Compound Interest keystone adds to both). A wave sent early (Send All, or Next while a wave is running) is a greed bet: its kills pay greed_bounty_per_stack more per wave of depth, its clear bonus greed_bonus_per_stack more. Supply: each tower of a type already standing makes the next of that type tower_cost_step dearer (walls and Salvage Drills have their own prices), so mixing types is cheaper than piling up one, and each tower of any type standing adds fleet_cost_step more, so the field fills slower and each tower is a choice. bounty_mult scales every kill bounty (2026-10: money came in faster than a full field could spend it). Drops are worth chaos_drop_mult while AXIS chaos is on (it was 3). The Spire mines and resource nodes pay only while a wave is on.

siege._note: Siege enemies (trait siege, VineEnemySiege.cs): walk the maze until a knot of towers is within range (a tower with at least min_crowd towers, itself included, within splash of it: a line along the route is safe, a block is not), bed down and shell the tower with the most towers within splash of it, every interval seconds, for hold seconds, then walk on (no new bed-down for cooldown seconds). A shell does damage x the climb's damage at its centre, half at the edge, to every tower in the splash, and bit_share of that to BIT. Procedural waves stop a siege surge at max_per_surge (the rest goes into health).

raids._note: Raiders (RaidManager): from start_wave on, while you hold resource nodes or have Salvage Drills standing, each wave sends raiders (one more every waves_per_extra waves, up to max) off the path to wreck them. Bosses, commanders, Ascendants and flyers never raid. Raiders without a gun hit for melee_mult times their shot.
